display.title: Haggadah in Yiddish 3a: Plagues at the Sea, Dayeinu, Rabban Gamliel and Hallel
display.summary_short: A Yiddish Haggadah class for children: counting the plagues at the sea, Dayeinu, Rabban Gamliel's Pesach, Matzah and Maror, and Hallel up to the second cup.
display.summary_long: Told in Yiddish to children, this class continues Maggid. Rabbi Yosi HaGlili shows that if one finger of Hashem brought ten plagues in Egypt, His whole hand at the sea brought fifty; Rabbi Eliezer counts each plague as four, making two hundred at the sea, and Rabbi Akiva counts five, making two hundred and fifty. The teacher then explains Dayeinu: fifteen kindnesses, from leaving Egypt to the Beis HaMikdash, each of which alone would have been enough to thank Hashem for, and the song is sung. Rabban Gamliel teaches that one must explain Pesach, Matzah and Maror: Hashem passed over the Jewish houses, the dough had no time to rise, and the Egyptians made our lives bitter. In every generation a Jew must see himself as if he left Egypt. The class ends with Lefichach and the first part of Hallel, how to hold the cup in the right hand shaped like a cup, the brachah Asher Ge'alanu with its Motzaei Shabbos change, and drinking the second cup while leaning.
display.lesson: Hashem did so many kindnesses for us that each one alone would deserve our thanks, and every Jew should feel as if he himself left Egypt.

advisories.note: The plague of the firstborn and the Egyptians drowning in the sea are mentioned.
